gaps.note: The supplier certification packet should cover every manufactured product and include a material assistance cost ratio. The PV module certification is not received, and no cost ratio calculation has been prepared.

The independent engineer's report should give an opinion on when construction began. It confirms only on-site work from January 12, 2026, and says it has not reviewed the transformer manufacturer's records.

The transformer manufacturer's letter asserts that work started December 22, 2025. It does not attach the binding contract or its terms. It also gives no evidence that the work was significant (costs, hours, records) and none on continuity after the transformer failed factory testing.
The prevailing wage and apprenticeship compliance report shows an apprenticeship shortfall. There is no record that the $370,800 cure payment has been made.
The cost segregation report is an estimate based on change orders through July 31, 2026. A final certified eligible basis is not yet available.

questions.prompt: Do you accept the off-site transformer manufacturing as the start of construction in December 2025?
questions.context: On-site physical work began January 12, 2026, and the notice to proceed does not count as physical work. A 2025 start rests on custom transformer core work from December 22, 2025, which is supported only by the manufacturer's letter. The transformer was later rewound after failing factory testing. With a 2025 start, domestic content qualifies at 47.8% and the foreign-entity rules do not apply. With a 2026 start, domestic content fails the 50% threshold, cutting the rate to 40% (credit $54,560,000 on $136,400,000). The foreign-entity rules would also apply, and failing them means no credit.

evidence.text: On-site physical work of a significant nature, beginning with pile installation for the tracker foundations, commenced on January 12, 2026.
Physical manufacture of the transformer, beginning with cutting and stacking of the custom core, commenced at our facility on December 22, 2025 and continued thereafter.
We have not reviewed the manufacturer's records and express no opinion on the tax treatment of off-site work.
If construction is determined to have begun in 2026, the applicable threshold would be 50% and the Project would not qualify at the computed adjusted percentage.
The main power transformer failed factory acceptance testing in August 2026 and is being rewound.

rfis.request: Provide the binding written contract for the main power transformer (Purchase Order CS1-MPT-001 dated December 10, 2025) with all terms, the manufacturer's production records, labor logs and costs for the custom core work starting December 22, 2025, evidence that work continued through the August 2026 rewind, and the beginning-of-construction memo offered by seller's counsel.
rfis.reason: A 2025 construction start rests only on off-site transformer work. The independent engineer has not reviewed the manufacturer's records and gives no opinion on it. The start date decides the domestic content threshold and whether the foreign-entity material assistance rules apply.

rfis.request: Provide proof that the $370,800 apprenticeship cure payment was made to the IRS, plus a bring-down prevailing wage and apprenticeship compliance report covering the full construction period through placed in service, with a recalculated labor-hour shortfall.
rfis.reason: The compliance report shows 13.2% apprentice labor hours against the 15.0% required, with no Good Faith Effort exception. The cure is only promised, and the report covers January 12 to September 15, 2026 only.

rfis.request: Deliver the PV module supplier's prohibited foreign entity certification and a material assistance cost ratio calculation for the Project.
rfis.reason: The module certification has not been received and no cost ratio has been prepared. If construction began in 2026, the rules apply and failing them means no credit.

rfis.request: Obtain an increase of the tax credit insurance limit to not less than 100% of the purchase price, and confirm the underwriter's approval and the added premium.
rfis.reason: The bound limit of $55,000,000 is $11,385,000 below the required $66,385,000. Even at the reduced basis, the implied purchase price of $63,767,000 exceeds the bound limit by $8,767,000.

rfis.request: Correct the insurance binder's project description from 132 MWdc to 135 MWdc, or explain the difference.
rfis.reason: Every other document states 100 MWac / 135 MWdc. The binder is the only outlier, which looks like a clerical error.

rfis.request: Confirm that the sponsor's model and credit amount have been updated to the $136,400,000 eligible basis, and provide the final eligible basis certification and final change orders when available.
rfis.reason: The cost segregation report excludes $5,600,000 of utility-owned network upgrades that the term sheet estimate included. The report also states that figures may change with final change orders.

rfis.request: Provide the transformer manufacturer's current delivery commitment and an updated EPC schedule showing the revised placed-in-service date.
rfis.reason: The independent engineer now forecasts placed in service on or about February 15, 2027 and considers a 2026 date unlikely.

rfis.request: Confirm that census tract 17135957900 appears on the most recent IRS list of coal closure and directly adjoining tracts that applies to the Project.
rfis.reason: The list in the data room is an excerpt from a 2023 notice. The site memo itself recommends checking against the current IRS list.

rfis.request: Provide the domestic content workpapers (manufactured product cost schedule and supplier cost data) supporting the 47.8% adjusted percentage.
rfis.reason: The percentage is only 2.2 points above the 2025 threshold of 45% and below the 2026 threshold of 50%, so the underlying cost allocation matters.

rfis.request: Explain why a Vermilion County siting ordinance for an unrelated Mural Energy, LLC project is in the data room, and confirm it does not relate to Cottonwood Solar I.
rfis.reason: The document concerns a different project and county from the Montgomery County site. Its presence should be explained or the document withdrawn.
